messages:
maya (support): FYI I have an open escalation from Acme — they reported a sudden p95/p99 jump after lyra-2.0 went live. p95 ~850ms, p99 spikes to ~2.7s on requests >4k tokens. Also they saw a small fraction of 401s and their dashboard shows a billing increase.

emily (sre): Thanks. Do we have a repro request and request-id? Any deploys that touched tokenization or auth yesterday evening? @luis @danny

maya (support): Repro: single prompt + 5k-token context, request id req_0a9f3c, reported start ~2026-03-16T23:12Z right after the lyra-2.0 rollout. Customer pasted their curl (redacted).

acme-billing-bot: Notice: account acme-prod token units increased 2.8x between 2026-03-16T22:00 and 2026-03-16T24:00. Spike correlated with lyra-2.0 traffic shift.

luis (runtime): We deployed lyra-2.0 yesterday. The tokenizer pipeline added an extra normalization pass (NFKC + join step) to fix quality on some unicode sequences. That may increase token counts and change KV cache behavior. I'll profile tokenizer + kv ops.

danny (ml): We also enabled a CJK fallback that normalizes certain codepoints — more CPU in tokenizer path. Could cause tail latency for long contexts.

maya (support): Customer curl snippet:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer xxxxx\" \
 -d '{"model":"lyra-2.0","input":"<5k tokens>","stream":false}'
```
They said most sessions are fine but these long-context sessions see the bad tail; 401s about 1% of requests during the window.

emily (sre): Hypothesis: token inflation causes more KV misses/padding and increases CPU, which cascades into timeouts/401s from retry/backoff. Can we repro locally with the exact payload and capture traces? @luis please stand up a canary.

luis (runtime): Spinning a local lyra-2.0 instance and replaying the payload now. Note: if token count increases we cross batching thresholds and buffer copies go up. Profiling tokenizer CPU and kernel times.

ops-bot: Rollout log: lyra-2.0 traffic 100% at 2026-03-16T23:05Z. Canary window showed small deltas; full traffic produced tail escalations.

danny (ml): If inflation is ~10-20% on long contexts, the runtime will see more tokens per request and higher KV accesses. Quick mitigation is to provide a model variant with the previous tokenizer behavior for customers needing strict latency.

maya (support): Acme needs a mitigation fast. Can we route them back to lyra-1.9 or spin a lyra-2.0 without the normalization?

luis (runtime): Two immediate choices: 1) route affected accounts to lyra-1.9 (fast and low-risk); 2) create lyra-2.0-legacy-tokenizer variant (disable normalization) as a targeted canary. I'll prepare routing overrides.

emily (sre): I've created a temporary route for acme-prod -> lyra-1.9 at 2026-03-17T00:10Z and loosened their token-rate throttle to avoid 401s from retry storms. Monitor enabled.

maya (support): Acme confirmed latency returned to baseline after being routed to 1.9. They want that as a temporary fix while we investigate.

luis (runtime): Local profile results completed: tokenizer CPU +18% on long inputs, extra memory copies from the normalization join step, and KV-cache miss rate +12% on long chains. Token counts inflated ~14% for the customer's payload. Primary culprit: tokenizer normalization.

danny (ml): Proposal: revert normalization in lyra-2.0 default, release a feature-flagged variant for normalization-enabled testing, and add an offline job to measure token-inflation per language/model prior to full rollout.

maya (support): Action items:
- keep Acme routed to lyra-1.9 (done)
- create lyra-2.0-legacy-tokenizer variant (luis)
- run token inflation metrics and per-lang heatmap (danny)
- finance to track billing delta and prep customer comms if usage persists (finance-bot)

luis (runtime): Pushed lyra-2.0-legacy-tokenizer canary and a feature flag to toggle normalization at serve time. Canary live 2026-03-17T02:05Z. Early canary metrics: long-ctx p99 down from ~2.7s -> ~0.9s.

finance-bot: Billing spike flagged and customer outreach queued if usage does not normalize after routing.

emily (sre): I'll keep a watch on the lyra family p95/p99 for 6 hours. If tail >2s again we'll cut traffic and consider full rollback. Also adding a postmortem ticket to document token-inflation checks in model rollout checklist.

maya (support): Customer confirms canary brought them back to expected latency. I'm closing the active escalation and will follow up with the customer rep.

luis (runtime): Next steps: bake token-inflation detection into canary metrics (alert if token/count ratio >5% vs baseline), add a pre-rollout synthetic suite with long-context traces.

danny (ml): We'll create the per-language token expansion heatmap and surface it to model-onboarding docs. Also run ablations to see if normalization can be optimized to avoid extra copies.

emily (sre): Postmortem items: add token-inflation safety gates, per-account routing quick-switch runbook, and add token-count telemetry to API traces so billing spikes can be correlated faster.

maya (support): Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
